title: Token Latency Atlas and Proactive Region Shed Simulator
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: build a reusable Token Latency Atlas (TLA) and an accompanying Proactive Region Shed Simulator (PRSS) so on-call and SRE teams can explore token-level SLI behaviors across regional topologies and evaluate admission control rules before rollout.

Context: We have multiple dashboards and SLI playbooks focused on per-token latency and regional failover, but they are fragmented: separate dashboards for p50/p95/p99, region rollups, and synthetic harnesses. This ticket consolidates a canonical data model (Token Path + stage timings), a visualization atlas for attribution, and a simulation harness that can inject synthetic microbursts, KV cache miss patterns, and cross-region latency skews to exercise our admission/circuit rules. The objective is to reduce ambiguity when tuning regional thresholds and to provide a repeatable simulation for canaries and postmortems.

Deliverables:
- Token Latency Atlas data model and event schema (prefix-aware, stage timestamps: ingress, routing, kv-prefetch, decode-start, decode-complete, egress).
- Grafana/Looker-grade dashboard panels: token path waterfall, per-stage quantiles by region/shard, prefix-impact heatmap, and adaptive-threshold suggestion panel.
- Proactive Region Shed Simulator (PRSS): lightweight harness that replays synthetic traces with controllable variables (burst size, sequence length distribution, kv-hit-rate, cross-region RTT). Output should feed same pipeline as production telemetry (tags to indicate simulated).
- A small set of admission policy regression tests that run PRSS scenarios and assert no-regression on SLO buckets (p95/p99 for token-level and request-level).
- Playbook snippets describing how to use the atlas to set region admission hysteresis and when to escalate to cross-region failover.

Acceptance criteria:
- Atlas schema documented in Confluence and compatible with existing telemetry pipeline (no special-case fields).
- Dashboards include at least 6 panels: token waterfall, stage quantiles, per-region skew histogram, prefix hotlist, simulated vs production overlay, and suggested threshold chart.
- PRSS can execute 5 canonical scenarios and emit labelled traces to staging telemetry; tests run in CI and assert SLO deltas < configured tolerances for non-failure scenarios.
- At least one runbook update and a 30-minute SRE walkthrough scheduled with on-call rotation after merge.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Simulation driving noise into production metrics if not tagged properly. Mitigation: PRSS writes with a reserved "sim" tag and is blocked from prod ingestion; staging-only by default.
- Risk: Dashboards become heavy and slow. Mitigation: panels will use pre-aggregated rollups and bounded sampling; ensure queries bounded by time-range and cardinality.

Notes on instrumentation approach:
- Prefer event model where every token emits a small set of stage timestamps instead of many derived metrics. This keeps flexibility for downstream quantiles and attribution.
- Sampling: full sampling for synthetic runs; adaptive sampling in prod (ex: 1% baseline plus 100% for tail traces flagged by the decoder when latency > p95).
- Correlate token traces with admission decisions and circuit state (include admit_score, circuit_id, and fallback_model tags).

Deliverable links (placeholders to be updated):
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Token+Latency+Atlas+Spec
- Grafana draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/token-latency-atlas
- PRSS repo (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/prss
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prss/pull/42
